question: Should OpenClaw accept this package-update boundary: preserve local packaged `dist` edits by default, expose `--reapply-local-overrides` for trusted replay, and require content inventories for future packages?
rationale: The code review did not find a concrete defect, but this changes upgrade behavior and filesystem trust semantics that automation should not approve without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve guarded replay boundary
options.body: Accept the preserve-by-default behavior, opt-in replay flag, content-inventory enforcement, and exact legacy package allowlist once the branch is refreshed.

options.title: Narrow to preservation only
options.body: Keep recovery-bundle capture/reporting but remove automatic replay until a separate owner-approved design lands.

options.title: Pause for broader release proof
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers require a full package release/update lane beyond the focused proof already supplied.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded replay boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the preserve-by-default behavior, opt-in replay flag, content-inventory enforcement, and exact legacy package allowlist once the branch is refreshed.
